concerns.concern: The g₂ decays are tiny and far from complete: fitted relaxation times exceed the measurement windows by factors of 3–20. As a result τ, β and contrast are strongly covariant, and β is poorly constrained, with no fit uncertainties, covariances or χ² reported.
concerns.quote: the data capture only the initial tail of the decay. In this regime, τ, β and the contrast A are strongly covariant

concerns.concern: A single τ is imposed for all aging times while β is allowed to vary. Any real change in relaxation time is then forced into β, which could artificially produce the reported β = 1 → 1.5 transition.
concerns.quote: Any genuine change in relaxation time with aging is then forced into β, which can artificially generate the β = 1 → 1.5 "transition".

concerns.concern: Joule heating at 4 mA (~8 mW) could cause thermal drift of the sample relative to the beam and shifts of the Bragg angle. Either would decorrelate speckle without any domain rearrangement, and no drift, peak-position or shift-corrected cross-correlation analysis is presented.
concerns.quote: Either effect decorrelates speckle or changes contrast without any domain rearrangement.

concerns.concern: The rise in cycle-to-cycle correlation over ~1000 cycles (~6000 s) may just reflect the system reaching a periodic thermal steady state rather than 'learning'. Control experiments are needed: gated acquisition with no current or a sub-threshold current, or cycling after thermal pre-equilibration.
concerns.quote: The rise of ΔG(n, n+1) could reflect the system reaching a periodic thermal steady state (reduced drift) rather than "learning".

concerns.concern: 'Deterministic switching' is not shown electrically. No electrical stochasticity metric (threshold distribution, delay jitter, On-resistance variance) is reported versus cycle number, so the title and abstract claims are not established.
concerns.quote: No electrical metric of switching stochasticity is reported versus cycle number

concerns.concern: A compressed exponent (β ≈ 1.5) is not a unique signature of jamming; it is common in aging or stress-relaxing out-of-equilibrium systems, and β = 1 does not uniquely mean liquid-like. Hallmarks of jamming such as dynamic heterogeneity, a control parameter or a diverging relaxation time are absent.
concerns.quote: They are not a unique signature of a jamming transition.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold (0.26 mA) case, which forms no filament, also shows 'jamming'. This contradicts the claim that electrical switching induces the jamming transition.
concerns.quote: Jamming is therefore not tied to filament formation, contrary to "electrical switching induces a jamming transition".

concerns.concern: ΔG(n, n+1) is min–max normalized, so a value of 1 does not mean identical configurations. The absolute change in correlation between the 'stochastic' and 'deterministic' regimes appears small.
concerns.quote: ΔG(n, n+1) is normalized to [0, 1] (min–max), so "1" does not mean identical configurations.

concerns.concern: X-ray beam-induced effects from hours of high-flux exposure (oxygen vacancies, heating, photo-induced metallization) are not addressed. These could themselves drive stabilization or decorrelation, so dose-dependence or fresh-spot controls are needed.
concerns.quote: Cumulative dose could itself drive configuration stabilization or decorrelation. A dose-dependence or fresh-spot control is needed.

concerns.concern: The beam is larger than the device and the coherence length is much smaller than the beam, giving low contrast. It is unclear how much of the signal comes from the filament region; static regions would dilute decorrelation and bias τ upward.
concerns.quote: Static regions would dilute the decorrelation and bias τ upward.

concerns.concern: It is ambiguous which Bragg reflection (200_M1 or 011_R) is tracked and whether they are resolved. Speckle changes could come from twin, M2/T phase or strain domains rather than metal/insulator domains.
concerns.quote: The attribution to "metallic and insulating domains" is therefore not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: The q-dependence of τ, needed to distinguish ballistic from diffusive dynamics, is not shown, despite the claim that domain speeds are obtained.
concerns.quote: This is not shown, despite the claim that "domain speeds are obtained".

concerns.concern: Each key result appears to come from a single run on a single device. There is no evidence of run-to-run or device-to-device reproducibility.
concerns.quote: There is no indication of run-to-run or device-to-device reproducibility, or of how many times the learning curve was observed.

concerns.concern: Jamming and learning are measured in different protocols. No β or τ analysis is done within the cycling data to show that the rise in correlation coincides with entering the jammed state.
concerns.quote: No β or τ analysis is performed within the cycling data to show that the rise in ΔG coincides with entry into the "jammed" state.

concerns.concern: The claimed train/reset functionality, in which sub-threshold currents erase memory and restore stochastic switching, is asserted but not demonstrated. No train → erase → retrain sequence is presented.
concerns.quote: no experiment shows cycling after sub-threshold erasure returning to low ΔG.

concerns.concern: The claimed trend that larger currents give slower transitions rests on statistically indistinguishable values. The shear-thickening analogy is therefore unsupported.
concerns.quote: relies on 1100 ± 600 s versus 1200 ± 500 s (statistically indistinguishable)

concerns.concern: For the 4 mA case, the sigmoid fit of β never clearly reaches the 1.5 plateau within the measurement window.
concerns.quote: For 4 mA, the sigmoid in Fig. 4 never clearly plateaus at 1.5 within the window.

concerns.concern: The activation energy is extracted from only two or very few temperatures. One of these is in a non-stationary regime during the transition, so the value is not robust.
concerns.quote: E_a = 230 ± 70 meV from so few points in a non-equilibrium regime is not robust.

concerns.concern: Comparing E_a/k_B to the melting point, with melting taken to mean all domains freely mobile, has no physical justification and should be removed or justified.
concerns.quote: An activation barrier for domain-wall motion has no direct relation to the melting temperature.

concerns.concern: It is unclear how slow changes in total Bragg intensity, expected as the metallic fraction changes, are separated from genuine speckle decorrelation.
concerns.quote: It is unclear how slow changes in total Bragg intensity (expected as metallic fraction changes) are separated from speckle decorrelation.

concerns.concern: The fit baseline (contrast A and the g₂ → 1 limit) is never reached in the data, and the manuscript does not state whether it is fixed or free.
concerns.quote: The baseline (A, and the g₂ → 1 limit) is never reached and is not stated as fixed or free.

concerns.concern: Eq. (1) uses an unconventional normalization (⟨I²⟩_t instead of pixel-averaged ⟨I(t₁)⟩⟨I(t₂)⟩), and the pixel/q-region averaging is not specified.
concerns.quote: Eq. (1) normalizes by ⟨I²⟩_t rather than the conventional pixel-averaged ⟨I(t₁)⟩⟨I(t₂)⟩.

concerns.concern: The possible role of Ga-induced defects as pinning sites for the 'learned' filament location is not discussed. All main-text switching data come from the irradiated device, with pristine results only in the SI.
concerns.quote: The role of Ga-induced defects as pinning sites (directly relevant to "learned" filament location) is not discussed.

concerns.concern: Simultaneous resistance and voltage traces during XPCS are not shown (notably for 0.26 mA, 1.7 mA and cycling), and the local device temperature under bias is not estimated.
concerns.quote: Simultaneous resistance and voltage traces are not shown

concerns.concern: Novelty is limited relative to existing work on memory effects (ramp-reversal memory, persistent metallic domains) and prior XPCS glassy dynamics. The paper should situate its results more carefully to delineate what is new.
concerns.quote: Memory effects are already well documented: ramp-reversal memory, persistent metallic domains, phase-boundary scarring (Refs. 9–11), and subthreshold firing (Ref. 45).

concerns.concern: The domain size estimate from the peak width conflates film thickness, strain inhomogeneity, mosaicity and instrumental resolution. It is also unclear whether the width is measured out-of-plane or in-plane.
concerns.quote: R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM = 20 ± 4 nm conflates finite film thickness (45 nm), strain inhomogeneity, mosaicity and instrumental resolution.

concerns.concern: Numerical values are inconsistent between text and figures: room-temperature τ, On-state τ, and the applied current values.
concerns.quote: Room-temperature τ is given as "8000 ± 3000 s" in the text but "81000 ± 3000 s" in Fig. 2c.

concerns.concern: The irradiation is described inconsistently (central region versus globally irradiated), and the two dose units are not reconciled.
concerns.quote: The main text says a "central 5×5 µm region irradiated", whereas Methods states devices were "globally irradiated".

concerns.concern: The text and figures do not match: the text refers to a non-existent inset in Fig. 3i, and the Fig. 1 caption labels its panels inconsistently.
concerns.quote: The text refers to "the inset (orange data)" in Fig. 3i, but no inset exists.
